title: One Ångström in the Yeast Starvation Bubble — Yoshinori Ohsumi's 1992 Microscope Watch of Vacuolar Autophagy, the 15 APG/ATG Mutants, Atg8–PE Lipid Anchoring (PDB 3VH4, 2ZPN, 2ZJD) & Human Beclin-1 / VPS34 PI3KC3-C1 Activation (PDB 4DDP, 9MHF)

teenKit.tldr: When yeast cells starve, they trigger a brutal self-eating survival mode called autophagy, dismantling their own internal parts to recycle into vital fuel.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding this cellular recycling program reveals how our bodies fight cancer, manage stress, and survive without food.
keyTakeaways: Christian de Duve coined 'autophagy' in 1963, meaning 'self-eating,' but the actual physical mechanism remained invisible for decades.
Yoshinori Ohsumi used clever yeast mutant strains lacking degrading enzymes in 1992 to finally watch starving cells fill up with bouncing autophagic bodies under a basic microscope.
Specialized proteins like Atg8 weld themselves to lipid anchors to build the membrane traps that capture and recycle cellular trash.

vocab.meaning: The cellular survival process where a cell eats its own internal parts to recycle raw materials during starvation.
The large storage and recycling compartment inside a yeast cell, acting like its central recycling plant.
A key ubiquitin-like protein that gets chemically bonded to fats to help build and seal autophagosome membranes.
A crucial human protein that helps trigger the creation of autophagy machinery and acts as a vital tumor suppressor.

quiz.question: What groundbreaking trick did Yoshinori Ohsumi use in 1992 to actually see autophagy happening in yeast?
options: He used a billion-dollar electron microscope to zoom in on individual atoms.
He starved yeast cells and used mutant strains missing internal degrading enzymes so the autophagic bodies piled up visibly.
He genetically engineered yeast cells to glow neon green when they ran out of sugar.
He heated the microscope stage until the yeast cells burst open.
quiz.explanation: By knocking out the vacuolar proteases, Ohsumi prevented the yeast from instantly destroying the self-eating vesicles, letting him watch them accumulate.

quiz.question: What does the Greek word 'autophagy' literally translate to in English?
quiz.explanation: Autophagy combines 'auto' (self) and 'phagey' (eating), perfectly describing how cells consume their own parts to stay alive.

quiz.question: Why is cellular autophagy considered the ultimate biological recycling program?
options: It turns old plastic waste inside the body into clean energy.
It shreds damaged internal organs and molecules down to basic raw materials to rebuild fresh survival machinery.
It causes cells to throw away all their DNA whenever they get tired.
It entirely replaces the need for a digestive system in mammals.
quiz.explanation: Cells break down their own non-essential or damaged components into basic molecular building blocks to construct vital survival tools during starvation.
